issues.detail: The Greek 'των ιουδαιων' (of the Jews) is translated as 'dân Giu-đa' (the people of Judah). In the New Testament context, 'Ioudaios' refers to the Jewish people/nation, whereas 'Judah' (Ioudas) refers specifically to the tribe or the kingdom. This changes the scope of the title from 'King of the Jews' to 'King of the people of Judah'.
